lines.label: Steel, aluminium, copper
lines.basis: Section 232, Proclamation 11021: 50% on the full value of articles made (almost) entirely of the metals, from 6 Apr 2026
lines.note: Derivative articles pay 25%; modelled at 50% for the whole chapter, which overstates chapter 73 (steel articles).
lines.verified: Verified: White House fact sheet on Proclamation 11021 (50% articles, 25% derivatives, UK 25%/15%).

lines.label: Steel, aluminium, copper — UK
lines.basis: Section 232, UK rate for articles made almost entirely of the metals
lines.verified: Verified: White House fact sheet on Proclamation 11021.

lines.label: Vehicles & parts
lines.basis: Section 232, Proclamation 10908 (cars Apr 2025, parts May 2025); trucks Proclamation 10984 (Nov 2025)
lines.note: Buses (10%) and non-covered items in chapter 87 are modelled at 25%.
lines.verified: Verified: White House fact sheet on Proclamation 10908 (25%); CRS IF12990 (trucks 25%, buses 10%).

lines.label: Vehicles & parts — EU, Japan, Korea
lines.basis: Section 232 deal rate: Column 1 (MFN) duty plus the 232 duty totals 15%
lines.note: Modelled as 15% minus the 2.5% car MFN = 12.5% additional.
lines.verified: Verified for Japan (EO 14345 text, White House) and Korea (Federal Register notice 2025-21940, govinfo). EU: same structure per notice 2025-18660, text not read.

lines.label: Vehicles — UK (quota)
lines.verified: UNVERIFIED: from secondary summaries only; official text not read.

lines.label: Vehicles & parts — Mexico, Canada
lines.basis: Section 232: USMCA vehicles pay 25% on non-US content only
lines.note: Coverage 0.76 reproduces the ~19% average tariff reported on cars from Canada and Mexico (USITC data via TD Cowen, Jul 2025).
lines.verified: UNVERIFIED estimate: the 25%-on-non-US-content rule is official; the 0.76 coverage comes from a press report of an analyst's calculation.

lines.label: Forced-labour 301 — 10% tier
lines.basis: Section 301, 91 FR 47318 (effective 24 Jul 2026); replaced the Section 122 10% surcharge
lines.note: USMCA goods are exempt. Coverage = 12% of Mexico (88% USMCA-compliant Jan–May 2026, CRS IF11175) and 15% of Canada (CRS IF12595: duties applied to about 15% of 2025 imports from Canada by value, including 232 goods, so an upper bound).
lines.verified: Rates cross-checked against several law-firm and trade-data summaries; Mexico and Canada coverage from CRS (IF11175, IF12595).

lines.label: Forced-labour 301 — 12.5% tier
lines.verified: Cross-checked against several summaries; China's 12.5% also in CRS IF12990.

lines.label: Forced-labour 301 — EU & Taiwan (10% cap incl. MFN)
lines.basis: Section 301, 91 FR 47318: tops the MFN rate up to 10%
lines.note: Modelled as 10% minus the 2.2% US trade-weighted MFN average (WTO) = 7.8%.

lines.label: Forced-labour 301 — Japan, Korea, Switzerland (12.5% cap incl. MFN)
lines.basis: Section 301, 91 FR 47318: tops the MFN rate up to 12.5%

lines.label: China 301 (Lists 1–4A and 2024 increases)
lines.basis: Section 301 China actions: Lists 1–3 at 25%, List 4A at 7.5% (2018–19), plus the May 2024 increases of 25–100% on EVs, batteries, semiconductors, solar cells, steel, aluminium, medical products and cranes
lines.note: Modelled as one average of 21.3 points, derived from CRS IF12990: its trade-weighted US average on China was 34% in Feb 2026 with the 10% Section 122 surcharge in force, minus that 10% and the 2.7% pre-war average (CRS, 2017) = 21.3. Check: 21.3 + 12.5 (forced-labour 301) + 2.7 = 36.5%, CRS's July 2026 figure. Ignores product exclusions.
lines.verified: Derived from CRS IF12990 (official Congressional research), Feb and Jul 2026 editions.

lines.label: Brazil 301 (25%)
lines.basis: Section 301 Brazil action (USTR, 15 Jul 2026; effective 22 Jul 2026), on top of the 12.5% forced-labour duty
lines.note: Excludes Section 232 goods; Brazil's own exemptions (agriculture, aerospace, pharmaceuticals, energy and more) are approximated by the forced-labour exemptions.
lines.verified: Verified: USTR press release (25% on certain goods of Brazil). Effective date from trade press.
